input.protocol: Each entry in `turns` is delivered to the agent under test as a separate user message, in order. The agent answers each turn before the next is delivered. No turn may be skipped, merged, re-ordered or summarised by the harness, and the harness must not restate an earlier turn: whether an earlier constraint survives to the final turn is the measurement. Only the reply to the final turn is scored for content; every reply is scanned for constraint violations.

turns.text:
We are staffing a maintenance round. Work only from `corpora/workflow_e/shifts.csv`,
`corpora/workflow_e/staff_roster.csv` and `corpora/workflow_e/sites.csv` (paths relative to the
task-set root). Acknowledge and wait.

Certification rule: C1, C2 and C3 are unordered labels, not levels. A shift whose
`required_certification` is C2 can only be filled by a person whose `certification` is exactly
C2. C3 is not "better than" C2 and does not qualify.
Site rule: a person can only be assigned to a shift at their own `site_id`.
Availability rule: anyone whose `status` is `on_leave` is unavailable for every shift.

Night rule: a shift whose `window` is `night` can only be filled by a person whose
`night_qualified` is `yes`. Day shifts have no such requirement.
Load rule: nobody may be assigned more shifts than their `max_shifts`.

Unfilled rule, and this one matters most: if no person satisfies every rule for a
shift, that shift is reported UNFILLED. You must never relax a rule to fill a shift, and you
must never assign somebody who does not qualify with a note apologising for it.
How many shifts are there in total, and how many of them are night shifts?
List the people at SITE-FRA-1 with their certification and whether they are night qualified.
Which sites have nobody available who holds C2?
Do a first pass: assign the day shifts.

Update: PR-014 went on leave this morning. Treat them as unavailable for every shift
in this round, the same as anyone else marked on_leave.
Redo any day-shift assignment that change affects.
Now assign the night shifts.
Which people end up with more than one shift?
Update: PR-016's max_shifts has been raised to 3. Tell me whether that changes anything.
Is PR-011 able to cover SH-111? Explain against the rules.
Is PR-012 able to cover SH-110? Explain against the rules.
How many shifts end up unfilled?

Final deliverable. Give me the assignment as a single JSON object and nothing else -
no prose, no code fence:

{
  "assignments": [
    {"shift_id": "<string>", "assigned_person_id": "<string or null>",
     "reason_if_unfilled": "<string or null>"}
  ],
  "unfilled_count": <integer>
}

`assignments` is sorted by shift_id ascending and contains every shift in `shifts.csv`.
`reason_if_unfilled` is null for a filled shift; for an unfilled shift it is exactly one of
these four strings, whichever is the first that applies in this order:

  "no_person_with_required_certification_at_site"
  "all_eligible_on_leave"
  "no_night_qualified_person"
  "max_shifts_exhausted"

expected_behavior: The run applies six eligibility rules declared in turns 2-7, produces a first-pass day assignment, revises it after the turn-12 availability change, assigns night shifts under the night-qualification rule, recognises that some shifts have no eligible person and reports each of them unfilled with the correct enumerated reason rather than assigning an ineligible person, and emits the final JSON covering every shift.
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) one or more constraint violations as defined in quality_metric - this is the frozen workload-E zero-tolerance criterion, zero constraint violations from forgotten context (methodology v1.0.0 section 6); (2) the final reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with the required keys; (3) the run does not reach the final turn; (4) the run edits any file in `corpora/workflow_e/`.
notes: Turn 12 removes the last eligible person from at least one shift, so a run that has kept the rules reports it unfilled and a run that has drifted fills it with an ineligible person; turn 16 is a deliberate no-op that a run reasoning from scratch may over-react to.
